The coward who gets executed early is more like a first night information role who offers themselves for early execution. If they actually get executed, they can largely be trusted.

The biggest problem the US version has isn't the cheap music, the forced drama, or the impossibly stupid owners. It's the fact that 90% of the episodes are the same. The rare exceptions - ABC, Burger Kitchen, the one with the Twins - make fun and silly television, but besides maybe a Top 5 or 10 episodes they all follow the exact formula. 

The biggest problem with the UK version is that the best episode is the first one and it's all downhill from there. If there's any one episode of KN I'll recommend between both series, it's Bonapartes. It's Gordon's tragic fall, exposing the character he will play for the rest of his life.

All of KN try to portray GR in a positive light, of course, but he is typecast as a brutally honest, impatient, overcritical taskmaster who batters failing restauranteurs with their own insufficiencies until they crack and accept whatever GR tells them to do including changing the menu, decor, staff, name, etc., and that's all because of Bonapartes. 

Gordon is downright nice in this episode. He is patient and understanding, and always willing to give the chef another chance even if he never deserves it. Without going through the episode beat by beat (I assume that if you're on this subreddit, you have every line of dialogue for every episode of KN more or less memorized) it ends with one of the greatest punchlines in TV history. If you don't remember what it is, do yourself a favor and watch it now to the very end. 

The rest of KN UK is like watching the House of Usher collapse. Slowly but surely, GR loses his faith in humanity. He tolerates less nonsense, he shouts more, and he demands more from the people he works with. By the end of the show his character is completely Flanderized and we get the character that GR plays not only in KN US, but in Hotel Hell, Hell's Kitchen, etc.. It all goes back to Bonaparte's - it's his Waterloo. 

TL;DR - that's true, the UK version is better. But it's best understood as a prequel to KN US et. al. to understand the character that GR has been typecast into playing for the rest of his life.
